page_title: DeepDeck: Open-Source Desktop Client for DeepSeek Harness

sources.entry: DeepDeck - Desktop AI workspace built on DeepSeek Harness for creating and reusing WebMCP tools for website tasks. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jo32/DeepDeck) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: DeepDeck
summary.one_liner: DeepDeck is an open-source, local AI desktop workbench that lets agents explore websites and save verified workflows as reusable WebMCP tools.
use_cases: Reusing website workflows such as search, reading results, and editing drafts
Having an agent learn a website once and save its operations as tools
Editing designs in web apps like Figma through agent-called tools
Browsing and summarizing Hacker News in a dedicated App
Building custom AI-assisted desktop apps with Vibe Coding
summary.what_it_does: DeepDeck is a desktop AI workbench built on DeepSeek Harness, with workspaces, modes, models, and a prompt in one flow. In its Browser + WebMCP feature, the agent explores and uses a website, then saves verified workflows as WebMCP tools that later tasks can reuse. Users can reuse tools a site already exposes via the Site Agent's WebMCP tab, or use WebMCP Builder to create missing tools. It also supports installable Apps (such as a Hacker News Reader and a long-form video investigation App) installed from Git sources after inspection and approval, plus a Vibe Coding workflow for building Apps with an agent. The page says DeepDeck keeps existing Harness settings and extensions compatible.
notable: Saves verified website operations as reusable WebMCP tools instead of repeating step-by-step clicks
Installable Apps with their own window, settings, and AI conversations, installed from Git source after inspection
Vibe Coding workflow where the agent edits an App and it hot-reloads
Signed and notarized installers for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs
caveats: Time and token savings depend on the site, tool design, and task; site changes may require tool updates
The changelog entry describes a source preview before its installer release
Building tools first requires exploration and verification effort
